messages:
oliver: Heads-up — kicking off canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC for sampler scheduling changes that touch batching. Quick API-contract Q: does `stop` always win over `max_tokens` in both streaming and non-streaming? want to avoid breaking customers relying on current semantics. :eyes:
sana: Which endpoint is this for? /v1/generate or the streaming endpoint?
oliver: Both. primary change is in runtime path that serves /v1/generate and the streaming socket.
maria: Current contract (from last RFC): stop sequences are honored immediately when generated. If `max_tokens` is reached first we truncate output and set a truncation flag (or `truncated: true`). Logprobs are returned only for tokens actually emitted; we don't fabricate logprobs for tokens that were stopped or would have been emitted after truncation.
kevin: Streaming nuance: do we ever emit a placeholder logprob or empty marker to indicate a stop? Some clients rely on a trailing marker.
maria: No placeholders. Streaming only emits token logprobs when a token is finalized. If a stop triggers, you get the stop token as part of the stream and then the terminal event — no synthetic zero/marker. Clients that depended on a marker should migrate to checking the termination reason field (`reason: "stop" | "max_tokens" | "error"`).
oliver: Can we add a small repro curl for the test matrix?
oliver: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model":"redwood-xxl",
  "prompt":"A
",
  "max_tokens":1,
  "stop":["
"],
  "temperature":0.0,
  "top_p":1.0,
  "logprobs":5
}'
```
sana: I'll add a unit/integration test: runtime/tests/stop_vs_max_compat.test.js. Will test non-stream + stream with temp=0 and temp>0 to ensure termination reason and logprobs behave. I'll link the PR here when ready.
jen: Docs note — we should add explicit language under API contract: "termination precedence: stop sequences > max_tokens; clients should inspect `termination_reason` and `truncated` fields, and not rely on synthetic logprob markers." @maria can you update the spec examples?
maria: Yep, I'll add example responses (non-streaming + streaming terminal event) and a short note about `logprobs` behavior. Also adding a Q&A blurb about `temperature/top_p`: sampling params do not change precedence — but they can affect actual tokens emitted (so tests should include deterministic and stochastic settings).
akash: Monitoring: I'll hook up canary metrics to the pattern detector (token-level mismatch rate) and watch for regressions in stop handling. Will roll back if mismatch > 0.5% on top-customer traffic.
kevin: One more: are we guaranteed to include `logprobs` when `max_tokens` truncates mid-token? A few libs expect final partial token info.
maria: We don't provide partial-token logprobs. We only provide logprobs for fully emitted tokens. If a token is truncated mid-generation it won't appear in the token array. We'll document that.
oliver: Great — plan: tests + docs + canary. If green, proceed with the wider rollout. Ping me on the PRs and I'll coordinate the canary window. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
